title: Mukhyamantri Balika Cycle Yojana (Bihar)
summary: Girls enrolling in secondary school (class 9) in Bihar Muralidharan & Prakash (AEJ: Applied, 2017): exposure to the Cycle programme raised girls' age-appropriate secondary enrolment by 32% and cut the gender gap by 40%; +18% girls appearing and +12% passing the secondary certificate exam; gains concentrated in villages far from a secondary school; more cost-effective than comparable South Asian CCTs. Method: triple difference (boys and neighbouring Jharkhand as comparisons) — NOT a randomised trial, contrary to how it is often described (including in this sweep's brief). RBI (Jun 2022) nonetheless listed the scheme in its 2022-23 'freebies' annex — the same table used to warn about fiscal risk. An in-kind transfer with one of the strongest causal evaluations in Indian social policy sits in the 'freebie' column: the category does not discriminate between effective and ineffective spending. Muralidharan & Prakash (AEJ: Applied 2017): the conditional in-kind transfer raised girls’ secondary-school enrolment and narrowed the gender gap, most where schools were far — the reference case for a state ‘distribution’ scheme with a rigorous positive human-capital evaluation; effect sizes not re-read in this sweep. Muralidharan & Prakash (AEJ: Applied 2017), triple-difference vs boys and Jharkhand: exposure raised girls' age-appropriate secondary enrolment by 32% and cut the gender gap by 40%; +18% girls appearing for the class-X board exam, +12% passing; effects concentrated in villages far from a secondary school (distance mechanism); more cost-effective than comparable CCTs. Innocent reading is the dominant one: a small, conditional, in-kind-equivalent transfer with a peer-reviewed causal effect, launched post-poll and 50 months before the next election; also used politically as "cycle wali sarkar" branding (analytic).

title: Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana
summary: women members of Jeevika self-help groups This is the closest launch-to-poll gap of any scheme in this file (~6 weeks from first disbursement to first phase of polling), targeted at >1 crore women shortly before an election the incumbent then won by the largest NDA margin in Bihar since 2010 — the case that best fits the 'schemes launched right before elections decide them' narrative on the numbers alone. Opposition parties and commentators characterised the scheme's timing as an inducement to vote; the government's position is that it is a continuation of Bihar's existing Jeevika self-help-group programme and self-employment policy, disbursed at the pace SHG verification allowed, and that the amount (₹10,000, below the ₹2,000 threshold the ECI treats as needing special scrutiny in isolated transfers) was consistent with the scheme design rather than newly invented for the poll. The largest single-day pre-poll transfer in this file: Rs 7,500 cr to 75 lakh women 10 days before the ECI schedule and ~6 weeks before polling; the incumbent went from 125 to 202 seats Bihar is absent from PRS's 12-state UCT list because MMRY is a one-time grant, not a monthly UCT — classification, not scale, kept it out

title: Chhattisgarh farm loan waiver (2018)
summary: indebted farmers (co-operative and some nationalised bank loans) This is the promise-delivered-immediately-after-winning pattern, not the promise-timed-before-an-election pattern: Congress waived the loans as literally its first act in office, five years before the election in which it then lost. Useful contrast case against any simple 'scheme timing determines outcome' reading — the same government that made good on this promise still lost the next election on a five-year time horizon. One of three same-week Congress waivers (MP 17 Dec, CT 17 Dec, RJ 19 Dec 2018) delivered as post-poll promises; RBI's IWG (Sep 2019) found waivers cluster near elections, damage credit culture and squeeze productive farm investment. All three governments lost in 2023 (MP's fell in 2020).
